steps.label: Do Now: AND (1 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: AND (1 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a range like this need AND, and not OR?Show the answer

Both edges must hold at the same time: the number must be above the bottom edge and below the top edge.

4 minutes. From 2.4.

1  DECLARE Age : INTEGER
2  INPUT Age
3  IF Age >= 13 AND Age <= 19 THEN
4      OUTPUT "Teen"
5  ELSE
6      OUTPUT "Not teen"
7  ENDIF
Total: 3 marks

steps.text: This is a different program. Do the same steps with your program.
steps.visual:
1  DECLARE Temp : INTEGER
2  INPUT Temp
3  IF Temp >= 20 AND Temp <= 30 THEN
4      OUTPUT "Nice"
5  ELSE
6      OUTPUT "Not nice"
7  ENDIF

steps.text: 30 is input. Line 3 has two conditions. 30 >= 20 is TRUE. 30 <= 30 is TRUE, because 30 is equal to 30. With AND, both are TRUE, so the THEN branch runs.
steps.visual:
1  DECLARE Temp : INTEGER
2  INPUT Temp
3  IF Temp >= 20 AND Temp <= 30 THEN
4      OUTPUT "Nice"
5  ELSE
6      OUTPUT "Not nice"
7  ENDIF
Output: Nice

steps.text: 31 is input. 31 >= 20 is TRUE. 31 <= 30 is FALSE. With AND, one FALSE makes the whole condition FALSE, so the ELSE branch runs.
steps.visual:
1  DECLARE Temp : INTEGER
2  INPUT Temp
3  IF Temp >= 20 AND Temp <= 30 THEN
4      OUTPUT "Nice"
5  ELSE
6      OUTPUT "Not nice"
7  ENDIF
Output: Not nice

steps.text: The smallest whole number for Nice: try the number in the first condition. 20 >= 20 is TRUE and 20 <= 30 is TRUE. One less does not work: it is not >= 20.
steps.visual:
1  DECLARE Temp : INTEGER
2  INPUT Temp
3  IF Temp >= 20 AND Temp <= 30 THEN
4      OUTPUT "Nice"
5  ELSE
6      OUTPUT "Not nice"
7  ENDIF
Smallest for Nice: 20

Year 8

Year 8 Term 1b Revision

Models, library functions, data types, IF and AND, OR, NOT

Think → Pair → ShareWhy check your notes now, before the questions start?Show the answer

A gap you find now can be fixed before it costs marks in a question.

  • 1 minutes. Today: the key facts for each topic, then exam questions in Data Bridge.

steps.label: Key Facts: Models and Data
steps.content:
Key Facts: Models and Data

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can a model give a wrong prediction even when its rules are right?Show the answer

The prediction is worked out from the data that goes in. Wrong or missing data gives a wrong prediction.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

  • A model is a simple computer version of a real system. It predicts what will happen.
  • A simulator is a model you use like the real thing, for example a flight simulator.
  • The parts: inputs (the data), rules (the calculations), outputs (the predictions).
  • Models are safer, cheaper and faster, and you can ask "What if?"
  • Garbage in, garbage out: good data is correct, up to date and complete.
  • The data requirements are the data the rule uses. A different job needs different data.

steps.label: Key Facts: Library Functions
steps.content:
Key Facts: Library Functions

Think → Pair → ShareWhy do you only need to know what goes in and what comes out of a library function?Show the answer

Someone else wrote and tested the lines inside, so you can use it without reading them.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

  • A library is code that is already written and tested, ready to use.
  • Call a library function: its name, then the values it needs in brackets. It gives back one value.
  • DECLARE, INPUT and OUTPUT are part of the language, not library functions.
CallWhat it gives back
MOD(20, 6)the remainder
DIV(20, 6)the whole number of times
ROUND(3.456, 1)the number rounded to 1 decimal place
LENGTH("Hat Yai")how many characters
UCASE("cat")the text in capital letters
RANDOM()a random number from 0 to 1

steps.label: Key Facts: Data Types and Constants
steps.content:
Key Facts: Data Types and Constants

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does "13" in quotes not act like the number 13?Show the answer

Quotes make a value text. The computer does not do sums with text.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

Data typeHoldsExample
INTEGERa whole number13
REALa number with a decimal part2.5
STRINGtext, in quotes"Cafe"
BOOLEANonly TRUE or FALSETRUE
  • DECLARE gives each variable its data type before it is used.
  • A value of the wrong type stops the program on that line.
  • A constant holds a value that never changes while the program runs: CONSTANT VAT <- 0.07
  • Change a constant in one place and every line that uses it changes.

steps.label: Key Facts: Conditional Statements
steps.content:
Key Facts: Conditional Statements

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must you test every branch of an IF?Show the answer

A mistake in one branch only shows when that branch runs, so each branch needs its own test value.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

  • Selection: IF a condition is TRUE, the THEN branch runs. If it is FALSE, the ELSE branch runs.
  • Comparison operators: = , <> (not equal), > , < , >= , <=
  • > and >=: >= is TRUE when the two values are equal. > is not.
  • Nested IF: an IF inside the ELSE gives three outcomes.
  • Check the highest number first. A high number also passes the lower checks.
  • Test every branch, and test the edge numbers.

steps.label: Key Facts: AND, OR and NOT
steps.content:
Key Facts: AND, OR and NOT

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is OR the right choice for a number outside a range?Show the answer

A number outside the range is below the bottom edge or above the top edge. It can never be both.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

OperatorThe whole condition is TRUE when
ANDboth conditions are TRUE
ORat least one condition is TRUE
NOTthe condition is FALSE (it swaps TRUE and FALSE)
  • Inside a range: Mark >= 50 AND Mark <= 100
  • Outside a range: Mark < 0 OR Mark > 100
  • AND does the same job as an IF inside an IF.
  • Put the values in and write TRUE or FALSE above each condition.
